exit_status_vocabulary.usage_return_definition: JMeter.start returns after help/version output or parser/IllegalUserActionException handling; numeric process status remains unasserted.
exit_status_vocabulary.numeric_status_rule: Numeric status is a separate exact process comparator field and is null/unasserted in this static corpus.

options.contract: Log4j2 configuration is selected before run diagnostics are compared.

options.last_resolution: JMeter.java comments mention LAST.log, but NewDriver receives -j directly and does not perform recent-project resolution; both forms remain planned literal-handling probes
options.contract: The paired single-quoted -j pattern is retained as an oracle probe. The research baseline names SimpleDateFormat, while the pinned NewDriver call-site formatter is not asserted by this static corpus; resolve the engine from the exact pinned source and observed output before implementing or comparing it.
Global and category-specific levels are ordered repeatable options.

comparison.process_exit_comparison: Compare the child process exit value exactly when an oracle run observes it; static descriptors keep process_exit null and process_exit_asserted false. Do not normalize numeric exits or infer them from sample success.
comparison.reason: NORM-CLI-001 compares canonical exit categories, termination behavior, and process exit as separate fields without treating localized prose as the sole oracle.

exit_contracts.termination_behavior: JMeter.start returns after printing the option output; no System.exit is called in the normal option path
exit_contracts.system_exit_observation: not observed; method-return category is planned

exit_contracts.termination_behavior: JMeter.start returns after printing the version banner; no System.exit is called in the normal option path
exit_contracts.system_exit_observation: not observed; method-return category is planned

exit_contracts.termination_behavior: normal CLI lifecycle returns without an explicit System.exit unless a separately selected force/stop policy applies
exit_contracts.system_exit_observation: not observed; process exit is a required comparator field

exit_contracts.trigger: ordinary assertion/sample failure during a completed CLI run
exit_contracts.termination_behavior: the plan completes normally while the failed sample remains in the result stream
exit_contracts.system_exit_observation: must not be inferred from sample success; process_exit remains a separate field

exit_contracts.trigger: unknown option or missing option argument reported by CLArgsParser
exit_contracts.termination_behavior: CLArgsParser error is printed with Usage and JMeter.start returns before initialization; no System.exit is called
exit_contracts.system_exit_observation: not observed; numeric status is intentionally not asserted

exit_contracts.trigger: IllegalUserActionException such as missing non-GUI plan, -e without -l, or report-only with -n/-r/-R/-l
exit_contracts.termination_behavior: the IllegalUserActionException catch prints Incorrect Usage and options, then JMeter.start returns; no System.exit is called
exit_contracts.system_exit_observation: not observed; numeric status is intentionally not asserted

exit_contracts.trigger: unreadable/missing plan, report input/output failure, or another uncaught startup Throwable
exit_contracts.candidate_status_basis: JMeter.java source calls System.exit(1) in the outer Throwable catch; this is not an observed child-process exit
exit_contracts.termination_behavior: JMeter.start catches Throwable, prints an error, and calls System.exit(1)
exit_contracts.system_exit_observation: not observed; candidate status is source-derived only

exit_contracts.trigger: remote host selection or worker failure
exit_contracts.candidate_status_basis: Only a client-side Throwable would reach JMeter.java System.exit(1); no remote/client process was run
exit_contracts.termination_behavior: retain the remote diagnostic category; if it escapes as a Throwable on the client, the outer catch calls System.exit(1)
exit_contracts.system_exit_observation: not observed; candidate status is not asserted

exit_contracts.termination_behavior: the client requests each selected remote engine to exit; worker System.exit(0) is controlled separately by jmeterengine.remote.system.exit
exit_contracts.system_exit_observation: not observed; client and worker process outcomes are separate fields

exit_contracts.property_transport: -J sets the local JMeter property before StandardJMeterEngine initializes its static stop-failure policy
exit_contracts.termination_behavior: false suppresses the worker-side System.exit(1) escalation when an immediate stop cannot stop all threads; true is the pinned default
exit_contracts.system_exit_observation: not observed; no stop-failure was induced by static validation

exit_contracts.property_transport: -G sends jmeterengine.remote.system.exit to selected remote workers; -J would affect only the client and is not equivalent
exit_contracts.termination_behavior: true permits a remote StandardJMeterEngine.exit path to call System.exit(0) after RMI returns; false leaves worker JVM shutdown to normal lifecycle
exit_contracts.system_exit_observation: not observed; no remote worker was started

exit_contracts.termination_behavior: ReportGenerator returns normally when generation succeeds; process_exit remains a separate comparator field

exit_contracts.candidate_status_basis: Report failure may escape to JMeter.java's System.exit(1) catch; this static corpus records no process status
exit_contracts.termination_behavior: an output/input failure escaping report generation reaches the Throwable catch and calls System.exit(1); parser-disallowed combinations remain usage-return instead
exit_contracts.system_exit_observation: not observed; candidate status is not asserted

future_observations.raw_artifacts: oracle-runs/cli-matrix/ (ignored and absent for this static corpus)
future_observations.process_exit_rule: The comparator must retain and compare process_exit exactly when observed, while this static corpus keeps it null and unasserted. Do not promote a numeric status from these descriptors; run the exact pinned oracle in a separate evidence-producing change.
